standard_prerequisites.use: Finite type and finite presentation ring maps, dimension of fibres of a morphism to the affine line, filtered colimits of rings and the behaviour of dimension along them, and the dimension bound for quotients by an ideal. The chain of reductions and the induction are retained.

core_obligations: Reduce to R -> S of finite presentation, then to R of finite type over Z, transporting the hypothesis that the fibres of f_a have dimension at most d through each reduction.

Run the induction on dim(R): cut out the complement of the distinguished open by an ideal I with dim(R/I) < dim(R), apply the inductive hypothesis to R/I -> S/IS, and combine the two thresholds with a maximum.

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce from an arbitrary finite type R -> S to the finite presentation case by presenting S as a quotient and using that the ideal is the union of its finitely generated subideals.
Reduce further to R of finite type over Z using a directed system of ring maps whose colimit is R -> S.

proof_roadmap.step: Finish by induction on dim(R) using an ideal cutting out the complement of the distinguished open, and take the maximum of the two thresholds.

spans.label: induction on the dimension of the base

difficulty_reason: For a finite type ring map R -> S and elements a, b, if the fibres of f_a : Spec(S) -> A^1_R have dimension at most d, then for all large n the fibres of f_{a^n+b} have dimension at most d. The proof is a long sequence of reductions that each remove a hypothesis: from arbitrary R -> S to finite presentation by writing S as a quotient and using that the ideal is a union of finitely generated ideals, then to R of finite type over Z by a filtered colimit argument with a dimension bound descending along the colimit, and finally an induction on dim(R) that peels off a component of the complement of a distinguished open and applies the inductive hypothesis to R/I -> S/IS. The final assembly takes the maximum of the two thresholds. What makes this non-routine is that the dimension condition must be transported through each of these reductions in the correct direction, and the induction needs the complement to be cut out by an ideal so that dim(R/I) < dim(R). Retained author proof at lines 8612-8777.
